faq.q: What is the maximum group size for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: The maximum group size depends on the boat's license. Most motor yachts in our fleet are licensed for up to 12 passengers, plus the skipper. Smaller boats like the Dubhe (5 pax) or Speedboat (6 pax) have lower limits. Always check the specific boat's capacity before booking.

faq.q: Are children counted in the group size limit?
faq.a: Yes, children of any age count towards the maximum passenger capacity. The limit includes everyone on board except the skipper. For safety and legal reasons, you cannot exceed the stated number of passengers, regardless of age.

faq.q: Can I rent a boat for a large group of 15 people in Marbella?
faq.a: No, our largest boats are licensed for a maximum of 12 passengers. For groups larger than 12, you would need to charter multiple boats. We can help coordinate two yachts sailing together from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: What happens if we exceed the group size limit?
faq.a: Exceeding the limit is illegal and unsafe. The skipper will refuse to depart if the group is over capacity. You may lose your deposit or be denied boarding. Always book a boat that matches your group size.

faq.q: Do all boats depart from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Yes, every boat in our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, Marbella's luxury marina. This includes all yachts listed, from the 8m Dubhe to the 29m Ferretti 94. Departure times are flexible.

faq.q: What is included in the rental price for a group?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. For Tier A boats, prices start at €749 for 2 hours.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks?
faq.a: Yes, you are welcome to bring your own food and additional drinks. The included beverages are non-negotiable but complementary. Many groups bring a picnic or order catering to the marina.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for a large group in 2028?
faq.a: For peak months (June–September), book at least 3–6 months ahead, especially for 12-pax yachts. For off-peak, 2–4 weeks is usually sufficient. Early booking secures your preferred boat and time slot.

data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental for 2028? One of the first questions you need to answer is: how many people can come aboard? Group size limits aren't just a suggestion — they're a legal requirement tied to each boat's license and safety certification. Whether you're organising a family outing, a stag do, or a corporate event, knowing the capacity rules will save you headaches at the dock. This guide covers everything from the 5-pax Dubhe to the 29-metre Ferretti 94, all departing from Puerto Banús.

Why Group Size Limits Matter in Marbella

Every boat in our fleet has a maximum passenger capacity set by its Spanish maritime license. This number includes everyone on board except the skipper. Exceeding it is illegal, voids insurance, and puts everyone at risk. The skipper will refuse to leave the marina if the group is over capacity. No exceptions. For 2028, the rules remain unchanged, but demand for larger yachts is rising — so book early if you need a 12-pax vessel.

Marbella Boat Rental Group Size Limits 2028: Legal & Safety Rules

Spanish maritime law caps passenger numbers based on the boat's construction, stability, and lifesaving equipment. For 2028, the limit for most motor yachts under 24 metres remains 12 passengers. Larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 (29m) also carry 12 pax due to their commercial license. Catamarans like the Lagoon 380 are limited to 10. These numbers are non-negotiable. The skipper is legally responsible for compliance. If you're planning a party or event, check the capacity before you book — it's the only number that matters.

Choosing the Right Boat for Your Group Size

For groups of 5 or fewer, the Dubhe or Mariah SX21 are perfect for a quick spin along the coast. For up to 8, the Bandido offers a sporty ride. The sweet spot for most groups is 9–12 pax, covered by the Astondoa 40, Azimut 39, and a range of 12-pax flybridge yachts. If you need the largest capacity, go for the Azimut 58 Flybridge, Mangusta 80, or Ferretti 94. All depart from Puerto Banús, so you're minutes from the Mediterranean. For pricing, Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, drinks, and snacks. Larger yachts like the Mangusta 80 have a minimum 4-hour booking at €4,719, which includes a free jet ski. For other boats, pricing is on request via WhatsApp.

What's Included in Every Charter?

Every boat rental includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. You can bring your own food and extra drinks. The skipper handles navigation and docking, so you can relax. For a full list of boats and prices, visit our Marbella boat rental hub.
